project_context: Design a system that can receive an electrical control signal and move the center of mass of the system from an origin point to a destination point and back on board the International Space Station (ISS).
conops: Displace the center of mass of the system from its origin to a set destination.
Return that point mass back to its origin.

requirements.text: Displace: The System shall be able to move a point mass from an origin point to a fixed destination point as seen in Figure 1. Note 1: The path shown in the figure is notional; the actual path is to be determined. Note 2: Assume that a link between the system output and the point mass will be designed separately (by someone else) and will match the needs of your design. Note 3: The origin point is (X, Y, Z) = (0 mm, 0 mm, 101.6 mm) or [0”, 0”, 4”]. Note 4: The destination point is (X, Y, Z) = (71.84 mm, 0 mm, -71.84 mm) or [2.82”, 0”, -2.82”].
Return: The System shall be able to move the point mass from the destination point back to the origin point.
The system shall execute FR1 accurately with +/- 2.5mm [0.1”] accuracy in every Cartesian direction.
The system shall execute FR2 accurately with +/- 2.5mm [0.1”] accuracy in every Cartesian direction.
The System shall be able to execute FR1 in no more than 30 seconds.
The System shall be able to execute FR1 in no less than 5 seconds.
The System shall be able to execute FR2 in no more than 30 seconds.
The System shall be able to execute FR2 in no less than 5 seconds.
The system shall be able to move a point mass of 3.6 kg perpendicularly to normal gravity (9.81 m/s2).
The System shall operate in an atmosphere comparable to that of Earth. Assume 21 degrees centigrade [70 degrees Fahrenheit], with low humidity, and pressurized to 100 kPA [750 mm Hg, 14.5 psi].
The System shall not contribute any particulates (e.g. dust) to the ISS atmosphere.
The System shall enclose all lubricated components to prevent lubricants from leaking into the atmosphere of the ISS.
The System shall not use more than 1.5 Watt-hours to support all operations. Note: Assume a maximum of 1 minute of operations.
